items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: we discussed this recently, Diz and I

ctx.x: Oh, I hadn’t heard about that.

Oh my dear, I can tell you stories. In any case, I remember walking at least — and we discussed this recently, Diz and I — at least five or six miles on a cold winter’s day with a trombone player who had terrible asthma I remember, and he played in sort of the Kid Ory type tailgate trombone between breaths of his asthma, or pants I should say, and we walked miles to go to a house where they had a record player and we could listen to this. And I’ve never forgotten, never ever forgotten. So we were enormously…
Was the fact that you had to go through that walking and it was hard to get the records, did it make the music that much more valuable to you do you think?
